learningObjective: Diagnose whether a kernel with low achieved occupancy is actually occupancy-limited or is memory-bound at high occupancy.

canonicalClaims.claim: In high-performance tile-based GEMM, low occupancy is a deliberate consequence of large tiles (high register + shared memory per block); if SM utilization is high and top stall is issue-slot pressure, raising occupancy by reducing tile size typically hurts performance.
conditions: Kernel uses large tiles that intentionally consume many resources per block.
SM utilization is near 100% and top stall reason is not memory.
nonImplications: Does not imply low occupancy is always fine.
Does not imply the kernel is at absolute peak; further Nsight sections must confirm.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Occupancy is a means to hide latency; SM utilization is the actual output metric.
Memory-bound is indicated by DRAM near peak; 25% is well below.
This is not how peak is calculated; SoL metrics involve different measurements.
High-performance GEMM legitimately uses many registers to hold tile fragments.
